signature.instructions:
Assign the support ticket to the squad that owns it: atlas, harbor, beacon, or quill.

When classifying tickets, remember the team ownership boundaries carefully: **harbor** handles performance issues (slow load times, timeouts), outages, API errors, and delivery failures. **atlas** handles billing, invoices, charges, refunds, and subscriptions. Do not assign performance or reliability tickets like 'pages take 30+ seconds to load' to atlas — that is a harbor concern. Always check whether the ticket describes a financial/billing topic (atlas) versus a system health/performance/availability topic (harbor) before assigning.

Feature requests, UI/UX enhancements (like dark mode), how-to questions, and usability tickets belong to **quill** — not atlas or harbor. Atlas is strictly for financial/billing topics (invoices, charges, refunds, subscriptions). Harbor is for system health/performance/availability issues. Quill covers everything product-feature and usability oriented. When a ticket asks to 'add', 'improve', or 'change' a UI element or requests a new capability, assign it to quill. Do not assign feature or UX tickets to atlas just because they mention a product surface like 'dashboard' — check whether the content is financial (atlas), performance/reliability (harbor), or a feature/usability/documentation request (quill).

When you see keywords like 'invoice', 'VAT', 'billing', 'charge', 'refund', or 'subscription', always assign to atlas — these are financial/document topics. Harbor is strictly for system health: slow load times, timeouts, outages, API errors, and delivery failures. Do NOT let the word 'wrong' or any sense of a 'problem' mislead you into picking harbor; the domain of the problem (financial document vs. system reliability) is what matters. For this ticket — 'Our VAT number is wrong on the latest invoice' — the topic is a billing document error, squarely in atlas territory.
